title: Reconciliation
summary: Purchased vs sold vs counted for each item: how it's worked out, why purchases must be logged, and how to read it.

blocks.text: For each item in a chosen window: **expected closing = opening count + purchased - sold**, compared with what was actually counted on the closing date. A negative variance means less is on hand than the math says there should be: waste, spoilage, theft or a miscount.
Why purchases are logged by hand

Sold (from {pos}) and counted (from your uploads) are automatic. Purchased only exists once it is logged, because {pos} doesn't share what was received. The fastest way is [Delivery Review](page:delivery_review): it suggests quantities for you to confirm.
This example uses one real item from your store, with its real opening count, sales and closing count. Type a purchased quantity to see how logging a delivery changes the result.

items: Search for the item, then enter the vendor, quantity and date. Unit cost and notes are optional.
For a whole delivery, **Bulk-log purchases from a CSV**: an item column (item name or item id) and a quantity column are needed; vendor, unit cost, received date and notes are optional.
Rows that can't be matched are skipped and listed, never guessed.

blocks.text: Until logging purchases is routine, expect most items to show a variance. That isn't real loss: nothing has been logged as bought yet, so any restock looks missing.
A simpler check: invoices or returns with no purchase logged from that vendor within a few days either side. It matches by vendor and date only, never by item. Each row links to the invoice file.
